risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The AR states the cash-to-digital shift places pressure on standalone transaction economics, pushing the Company towards assisted non-cash BFSI services.
- Greater dependence on banking, insurance and lending partners can increase concentration risk; a partner decision can affect service availability across the distributed platform.
- A franchisee lapse can create regulatory and reputational consequences given the Company's reliance on the Master Franchisee and Franchisee model for last-mile distribution.
- Growing technology and data infrastructure builds Intellectual Capital but can increase cyber risk, energy use and vendor dependency.
- Expanding Vortex products and AMC adds Intellectual, Manufactured and Financial Capital but may require inventory, working capital and after-sales capability, creating quality and after-sales obligations.
- The Company's breadth across regulated financial services, technology platforms, franchisee network, ATM infrastructure and partnerships makes risk interdependent — a technology incident can affect customer trust, and a partner decision can affect service availability.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Shift focus from network scale/reach towards higher-margin BFSI and non-cash services, yield per Kendra and platform economics.
- Increase emphasis on BFSI-led offerings such as account opening, loan products, insurance, fixed deposits, mutual funds and NPA recovery.
- Grow Vortex Engineering's banking-automation business (ATM manufacturing, Mini/Android ATMs, Perfo, AMC) as a technology-led revenue layer.
- Use BharatEasy as the digital (O2O) extension of the Kendra network rather than a standalone app.
- Scale via the asset-light Master Franchisee and Franchisee model, with training, compliance and …
